lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- How It Actually Gets Done
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Victor Garcia Ferreira de Oliveira | Lesson 7 -- How It Actually Gets Done

listenings.text: People imagine that the hard part is building the thing, and I understand why, but it is not what happens. There are four stages here, and nothing moves to the next one until the previous one has been signed off. That rule was not invented by somebody who likes rules. It was invented after a week in which two stages ran at the same time and neither of them was finished. So, design first, and the design is signed off before a single line is written. Then the code is submitted and it is reviewed, and this is where it actually gets slow. The bottleneck is not the building. It is the waiting, because nothing is approved until two people have read it, and those two people have their own week. New people are always surprised by that. They expect the slow part to be the work. And the last thing, which is the one I would tell a student: almost all of this is behind the scenes. The button somebody sees on a Tuesday took an afternoon. Everything underneath it had been built over three weeks, and nobody outside the team will ever know that.

The first thing somebody submits to me usually comes back with about twenty comments on it, and I want to say very clearly that the number means nothing about the person. Mine had more. Twenty comments is what a first submission looks like, every single time, and if it came back with two I would assume nobody had read it properly. What I try to do is write about the work and not about the person, and the reason is simple: the work can be changed and the person cannot be changed by a comment. So every line I write has to be something the writer can act on tomorrow morning. Not this is confusing, but this name will confuse the next person who opens the file. And there is one reaction that worries me, and it is not the one people expect. It is silence. Somebody who argues with a comment is learning, and I like those reviews. Somebody who says nothing at all and quietly changes every single line has understood none of it, and they will submit the same thing again next month.
